pelage_geometry_and_topology.patch_morphology: Large, non-uniform polygonal regions with high-contrast edge gradients. Geometry transitions from large, stable polygons on the flank to smaller, more fragmented shapes on the posterior hindquarter. Pixel values within several patches on the upper flank show central lightening, likely due to specular reflection or sunlight exposure.
pelage_geometry_and_topology.corridor_network: Interconnected light-colored network forming the negative space between patches. Topology consists of junction nodes with tri-radial and quadri-radial branching. Pathway thickness remains relatively constant across the mid-body but exhibits localized narrowing and higher density at the hip transition.

dorsal_ridge_profile.edge_serration: Consistent 1D jagged silhouette along the cervical and thoracic dorsal line. The mane exhibits a high-frequency, low-amplitude serrated profile against the sky and background vegetation.

other_distinctive_markers: Presence of two avian organisms (oxpeckers) on the dorsal-lateral region of the neck and shoulder, causing localized pixel occlusion of the pelage pattern.
